data_collected.text: Name, date of birth, contact details, previous academic records, category certificate (if applicable) and a photograph.

purposes.text: Admission, academic records, examinations and certificates.
Publicity: your name, photograph and event videos in brochures, social media posts and advertising campaigns.

recipients.text: No recipients are named. Publicity use means the public will see your name and image.

choices_and_withdrawal.text: One signature covers both enrollment and publicity, and signing is mandatory to register.

unknowns: How long records and publicity material are kept.
Whether you can later withdraw from publicity use.
Who to contact with privacy questions.

data_inventory.data_category: Enrollment data (name, date of birth, contact, academic records, category certificate, photograph)

consent_dimensions.explanation: Both the enrollment and publicity purposes are stated specifically.
Publicity use is combined with enrollment in one declaration.
There is a single signature and no separate box or choice for publicity.
The form asks for a signature, which is a clear action. The problem is what the signature is bundled with.
The form does not mention withdrawal.
No retention periods are given, and no recipients beyond publicity channels are named.
Optional publicity is made a condition of mandatory registration.

findings.title: Publicity use bundled with mandatory registration
findings.explanation: Advertising use of your name, photograph and videos is not needed to enroll, yet it sits in the same declaration that you must sign to register. You cannot agree to enrollment without also agreeing to publicity.

quotes.quote: using my name, photograph and video recordings of campus events in brochures, social media posts and advertising campaigns
Signing this declaration is mandatory to complete registration.

targeted_questions.question: Can I register without agreeing to the use of my photo and videos in advertising?
targeted_questions.why_it_matters: Enrollment should not depend on optional publicity.

targeted_questions.question: How can I withdraw from publicity later?
targeted_questions.why_it_matters: Images on social media can be hard to remove once published.

next_steps.action: Before signing, ask for a separate publicity choice in writing.
If the Institute offers a publicity opt-out form, consider using it.
Ask the admissions office for a separate publicity choice, or whether you can strike out the publicity part and still register. Keep a copy of anything you sign.
Ask how you can withdraw from publicity use later, and how material already published is handled.
Ask how long your records and any publicity images are kept.
Ask the Institute for its privacy or grievance contact.

evidence.text: Northfield Institute of Management: Student Registration Form, Data Declaration
SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION DOCUMENT: Northfield Institute of Management is a fictional institution invented for ConsentGuard demos. This is not a real form.
For enrollment we collect your name, date of birth, contact details, previous academic records, category certificate (if applicable) and a passport-size photograph.
Your information will be used to process your admission, maintain academic records, conduct examinations and issue certificates.

By signing below, I consent to the Institute using my personal information for enrollment and academic administration, and to the Institute using my name, photograph and video recordings of campus events in brochures, social media posts and advertising campaigns.
Signing this declaration is mandatory to complete registration.

legal_sources.title: Notification G.S.R. 843(E) appointing commencement dates for the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
legal_sources.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
legal_sources.summary: On publication: s.1(2), s.2, ss.18-26, s.35, ss.38-43, s.44(1) and (3). One year after publication: s.6(9) and s.27(1)(d). Eighteen months after publication: ss.3-5, s.6(1)-(8) and (10), ss.7-17, s.27 (except (1)(d)), ss.28-34, 36, 37 and s.44(2).
legal_sources.applicability_notes: Controls which DPDP Act duties are in force on a given date.

legal_sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, rule 3 - Notice given by Data Fiduciary
legal_sources.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
legal_sources.summary: The notice must be understandable independently of other information; give in clear and plain language an itemised description of personal data and the specified purpose(s); and give a link and other means to withdraw consent with ease comparable to giving it, exercise rights, and complain to the Board.
legal_sources.applicability_notes: Commences eighteen months after publication of the Rules.

legal_sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, rule 8 - Time period for specified purpose deemed no longer served
legal_sources.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
legal_sources.summary: Specified classes of Data Fiduciaries must erase data after periods set in the Third Schedule (with 48-hour prior intimation); all Data Fiduciaries must retain processing logs and associated data for at least one year for purposes in the Seventh Schedule.
legal_sources.applicability_notes: Commences eighteen months after publication of the Rules. Note the one-year minimum log retention: a notice that mentions retaining some records for a year is not necessarily over-retention.

legal_sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 13 - Right of grievance redressal
legal_sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India; text hosted by MeitY
legal_sources.summary: A Data Principal has the right to readily available means of grievance redressal provided by the Data Fiduciary.

legal_sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 5 - Notice
legal_sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India; text hosted by MeitY
legal_sources.summary: A consent request must be accompanied or preceded by a notice describing the personal data and purpose, how to exercise withdrawal and grievance rights, and how to complain to the Board; option to access the notice in English or an Eighth Schedule language.
legal_sources.applicability_notes: Commences eighteen months after G.S.R. 843(E). Applies to consent requests, not to processing on other grounds.

legal_sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 6 - Consent
legal_sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India; text hosted by MeitY
legal_sources.summary: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action, limited to data necessary for the specified purpose (6(1)); illustration: contact-list access is not necessary for a telemedicine service. Withdrawal must be comparable in ease to giving consent (6(4)).
legal_sources.applicability_notes: Commences eighteen months after G.S.R. 843(E). Relevant only where consent is the basis of processing.

legal_sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 8(7) - Erasure
legal_sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India; text hosted by MeitY
legal_sources.summary: Unless retention is necessary to comply with law, personal data must be erased on withdrawal of consent or once it is reasonable to assume the specified purpose is no longer served, whichever is earlier.

limitations: ConsentGuard explains and assesses the supplied text only. It does not know whether the organisation actually follows its policy.
This is a consumer-education prototype, not legal advice, a compliance certification, or a security scan.
Severity and confidence labels are prototype governance heuristics, not statutory classifications.
A privacy notice alone cannot show how a consent screen behaves (for example, whether boxes are pre-ticked).
Legal sources are limited to the India registry verified on the date shown; laws and commencement dates can change.
No consent-screen text was supplied, so interface behaviour was not assessed.
